from.place: proof step 1: sections on standard intersections are Laurent monomials and the Cech complex splits by exponent vector

title: Cech sections of a projective-space twist decompose into Laurent monomials
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge1$, $d\in\mathbf Z$, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$ with standard opens $U_i=D_+(x_i)$, and $\mathcal O_P(d)$ the twisting module [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. For every nonempty $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n\}$, the sections of $\mathcal O_P(d)$ on $U_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}U_j$ identify with the free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x^e=\prod_ix_i^{e_i}$ with $\sum_ie_i=d$ and $e_i\ge0$ for $i\notin J$, and under these identifications every restriction map $\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal O_P(d))\to\Gamma(U_{J'},\mathcal O_P(d))$, $J\subseteq J'$, is the inclusion of monomial bases. Consequently the alternating Cech complex of $\mathcal O_P(d)$ on this cover [lem-pc-alternating-cech-computes] is the direct sum, over $e\in\mathbf Z^{n+1}$ with $\sum_ie_i=d$, of the subcomplexes $C_e^\bullet$ whose degree-$p$ basis is the set of $J$ with $|J|=p+1$ and $J\supseteq N_e=\{i:e_i<0\}$.

source.place: Tag 01XS, label lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, proof: Cech terms and grading

proof.text: On an intersection $U_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}D_+(x_j)$, the twisting module is obtained by gluing the chart generators $e_i^{(d)}$ with transition rule $e_i^{(d)}=(x_i/x_j)^d e_j^{(d)}$.  A section written in the chart $U_i$ is therefore a homogeneous degree-zero fraction $(x^e/x_i^d)e_i^{(d)}$, where $\sum_i e_i=d$ and the only coordinates allowed in denominators are those indexed by $J$.  Equivalently, the section is the Laurent monomial $x^e$ with $e_j\ge0$ for every $j\notin J$.  The Laurent monomials are linearly independent over $A$ in the localized polynomial ring, so they form the asserted free $A$-basis.

source.place: Tag 01XS, label lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, proof: Cech terms and grading

proof.text: If $J\subseteq J'$, restriction is localization at the additional coordinates in $J'\setminus J$.  It sends each Laurent monomial $x^e$ to the same monomial and only removes the nonnegativity requirement for the newly inverted coordinates; hence, under the displayed bases, the restriction map is the inclusion of the corresponding monomial basis.

source.place: Tag 01XS, label lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, proof: Cech terms and grading

proof.text: The alternating Cech complex is indexed by nonempty subsets $J$ (equivalently, strictly increasing index tuples).  Since every restriction preserves the exponent vector $e$, the differential preserves $e$ as well.  Grouping the basis vectors with the same exponent gives the direct sum over all $e\in\mathbf Z^{n+1}$ with $\sum_i e_i=d$; in degree $p$ the summand $C_e^\bullet$ has basis exactly the subsets $J$ of cardinality $p+1$ containing $N_e=\{i:e_i<0\}$.
